subject: Architecture
title: The Parthenon: Perfection in Stone
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Parthenon: Perfection in Stone usable.

hook.text: The Parthenon looks perfectly straight. In reality, almost nothing about it is truly straight.

buildup.text: Columns lean inward, the floor curves upward, and every surface has subtle adjustments for the human eye.

discovery.text: These 'optical refinements' counteract visual illusions — making straight lines that look straight.

twist.text: The Parthenon survived 2,000 years intact. Then the Venetians bombed an Ottoman gunpowder store inside it.

climax.text: Lord Elgin removed half the sculptures in 1801. Greece has demanded their return for over 200 years.

punchline.text: The most perfect building was imperfect on purpose.

quiz.question: Why do the Parthenon's columns lean slightly inward?
options: To counteract optical illusions and appear perfectly straight
Because the builders made measurement errors
